analysis.title: Novartis (NOVN.S) MNM 2026 - new mid-term guide implies c.3% upside, focus likely on filling the $20bn post 2030 gap
key_insights: Novartis held its 2026 Meet the Management event on Nov 19. It reiterated the 2025-30 mid-term group net sales target of +5-6% cc CAGR and the 2029 core operating income margin guide of 40%+.

Novartis rolled its mid-term guide forward to 2026-31 with a sales CAGR of +5% in cc, against consensus of 4.3% CAGR. GS says this is broadly in line with its own estimates and implies c.3% upside risk to company consensus sales and operating profit in 2031.

Adjusting the 2026 sales guide mid-point for 2027 FX assumptions implies c.3.1% upside to 2031 consensus sales ($71,747mn implied mid-point vs $69,616mn consensus) and c.2.4% upside to 2031 core operating income ($29,058mn vs $28,387mn).

Management continues to expect mid-single-digit % CAGR growth after 2030, against consensus at -1%. Patent expirations create a c.$20bn sales gap between management expectations and consensus. GS expects how Novartis plans to fill this gap to be the key focus of the event.

Peak sales guidance was raised for Kesimpta to $8bn+ (from $6bn+, consensus $7.4bn), Leqvio to $5bn+ (from $4bn, consensus $4.8bn) and Scemblix to $5bn+ (from $4bn+, consensus $4.9bn). Consensus already sat broadly at these levels. Zolgensma/Itvisma got new $3bn+ guidance (previously multi-bn, consensus $2.2bn).
Novartis cites 9 de-risked in-market assets with peak sales potential of $3-10bn, 35+ submission-enabling readouts through 2031, and 30+ pipeline assets supporting MSD growth beyond 2031.

GS says upside to consensus estimates is a positive and has historically taken around 6-12 months to work into consensus. It believes this is broadly in line with investor expectations going into the event.

GS believes further M&A and additional clinical proof points are required before the gap between long-term targets and consensus fully closes. The event could start to narrow it with discussion of new assets.

GS flags that the 2027 clinical catalyst path looks light. Other focus areas are the drivers of the peak sales upgrades, assumptions in the 2026-31 guide including the Cosentyx loss of exclusivity, and capital allocation policy.
GS rates Novartis Sell with a 12-month price target of CHF 113 / $136 per ADR. That implies 14.1% downside for NOVN.S (CHF 131.48) and 12.4% for NVS ($155.21). The target blends DCF and P/E 50:50.

GS estimates 2026E revenue of $56.5bn (+3.6%) and 2027E of $60.3bn (+6.8%). EPS is $9.01 in 2026E (+1.2%) and $10.08 in 2027E (+11.9%). Net debt/EBITDA rises to 1.7x in 2026E, with $14.3bn of acquisitions in the cash flow forecast.

market_movers.rationale: GS keeps its Sell on Novartis with a $136 ADR target, 12.4% below the $155.21 price. The mid-term guide upgrade is largely anticipated by consensus, and a c.$20bn post-2030 sales gap remains.

sector_views.rationale: The note covers a single company. It carries no sector-wide stance.

earnings_insights: The 2026-31 guide of +5% cc sales CAGR compares with consensus of 4.3% CAGR (consensus estimate, not a reported figure). GS puts the implied 2031 net sales mid-point at $71,747mn vs consensus of $69,616mn, a 3.1% difference.
Implied 2031 core operating income mid-point is $29,058mn vs consensus of $28,387mn, a 2.4% difference. The margin guide is ~40%+, with 40.5% in 2026 and 40.8% FX adjusted.

GS forecasts: 2026E EPS $9.01 and 2027E EPS $10.08 (basic, pre-exceptionals $9.09 and $10.17). Quarterly EPS estimates are $2.19 for 12/26E, $2.21 for 3/27E and $2.57 for 6/27E, with $2.45 for 9/26 shown in the key-data table. All of these are GS estimates.
GS 2025 actuals: revenue $54,532mn, EBIT $21,889mn, EPS $8.91. 2026E EBIT growth is 1.7% and 2027E is 9.4%.
risk_factors: Upside risks to the Sell view and price targets: ongoing positive earnings momentum, stronger-than-anticipated sales from key franchises, unforeseen pipeline success, and capital allocation priorities including business development and share buybacks.
The wave of patent expirations after 2030 and the Cosentyx loss of exclusivity create the c.$20bn gap between management's long-term growth guidance and consensus.
GS expects a light 2027 clinical catalyst path.

tension_points.bull_case: Management guides to MSD % CAGR post 2030, backed by 9 de-risked in-market assets with $3-10bn peak potential, 35+ submission-enabling readouts through 2031 and 30+ pipeline assets, with most launches protected in the US into the 2030s.
tension_points.bear_case: Consensus sits at -1% post-2030 growth because of patent expirations, leaving a c.$20bn sales gap. GS says further M&A and additional clinical proof points are required before it closes.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Evidence that the gap is closing, such as discussion of new assets at the event, further M&A and additional clinical proof points. GS says these are needed before the gap will fully close.

theme_stances.key_argument: Further M&A and additional clinical proof points are required before the gap between management's long-term targets and consensus fully closes.
theme_stances.evidence: further M&A and additional clinical proof points are required
